https://sortyard.ai/spec/agent.schema.js.description: Agent / Worker: an executor (§3.7) — harness type, model policy, credential pool ref, tool set. Workers run as Kubernetes Jobs, one stage per pod, with no GitHub/tracker access by default, and never push: they produce a branch/patch in a clone taken from a repo Mirror.
https://sortyard.ai/spec/agent.schema.js.title: Agent

https://sortyard.ai/spec/alert.schema.js.description: Alert / Finding: monitoring output (§3.8) — stillness watch (oldest unowned work, oldest logjam, merges/day, owner-pointed-out count), deploy-down detection (a product with no green deploy on current head is DOWN, reported in those words), and drift detection (definitions vs live state, plan vs board vs done-vs-live).

examples.summary: Rove is DOWN: no green deploy on current head.

task_id.description: Task the finding was filed as, if any.

https://sortyard.ai/spec/alert.schema.js.title: Alert

https://sortyard.ai/spec/archetype.schem.description: A versioned template bundle (§3.2): default workflows, roles, contracts, skill slots, eval suites, replica definition, definition-of-done. Shipped archetypes: saas-product, infrastructure; candidates: inception, opportunity-portfolio.

replica_definition.description: Definition of the replica used for build-stage adversary review (§3.6 replica_required).

https://sortyard.ai/spec/archetype.schem.title: Archetype

https://sortyard.ai/spec/audit-log.schem.description: One entry of the AuditLog (§3.9): every UI/API mutation — who, what, when, before, after.
https://sortyard.ai/spec/audit-log.schem.title: AuditLogEntry

https://sortyard.ai/spec/chain.schema.js.description: Chain / Run: one task's passage through a workflow (§3.3), the ordered StageRuns. Pins the workflow version it started on and runs it to completion (§5.1a). Chains advance automatically; stalls are explicit Escalation objects. Revision rounds cap at four.
https://sortyard.ai/spec/chain.schema.js.title: Chain

absent_state.description: Named behaviour when the thing cannot run or its input is absent (§1.6; mandatory for eval gates).

actor.description: Who did something: a human operator, an agent (service account), the system, or a sensor.

content_hash.description: Content hash; definitions and context packets are content-addressed (§5.1c, §3.7a).

definition_base.description: Definitions live in git and are materialised into the DB as immutable, content-hashed versions (§5.1).

source.description: Where the version was materialised from (§5.1: git mode or DB-only mode).

id.description: Stable identifier of an object. Opaque to clients.

object_base.description: Fields every workspace-scoped object carries. workspace_id exists from day one (§3.1).

ref.description: Reference to another object by its id.

scope.description: Where a policy or definition applies (§3.6).

secret_ref.description: Pointer to a Secret object (secret.schema.json). Never a value (§3.7a).

version.description: Definition version label. Versions are immutable once materialised (§5.1).

versioned_ref.description: Reference to an immutable version of a definition (pinning, §5.1a).

https://sortyard.ai/spec/common.schema.j.description: Shared building blocks for every Sortyard domain object: identifiers, references, timestamps, content hashes, the tenancy field and the definition/state base shapes (design §3, §5.1). Not an object itself.
https://sortyard.ai/spec/common.schema.j.title: Sortyard common definitions

https://sortyard.ai/spec/conductor-confi.description: The Conductor is the deterministic scheduler service, not an object; its configuration is (§3.4): pickup policy ref, poll interval, claim lease duration, stall thresholds. Also carries the stacked admission caps of §3.7b that sit above individual lanes (see NOTES.md).

reserved_rush_slot.description: Rush is admitted first but never preempts a running job.

pickup_policy_ref.description: PrioritizationPolicy used for the claim sequence.

https://sortyard.ai/spec/conductor-confi.title: ConductorConfig

https://sortyard.ai/spec/context-recipe..description: Defines, per project/worktype/role, which domain objects, documents and skills an agent's context packet includes, in what order, with what token budget (§3.7a Context Assembly). Built from an allowlist, never retrieval over a vault. Every StageRun records the exact packet (hash + content ref); the goldfish test is a checkable property.

goldfish_test.description: Packet + referenced dossier must suffice for a zero-context agent.

worktype.description: Workflow (and optionally stage) this recipe serves.

https://sortyard.ai/spec/context-recipe..title: ContextRecipe

https://sortyard.ai/spec/credential-cust.description: Per-credential custody class (§3.7a): store (secrets store), cli-owned-files (0600 files on a dedicated volume, because the CLIs own the refresh lifecycle and write tokens back), or operator-side (outside the cluster). Moving a long-lived GitHub write credential into the cluster requires explicit approval and is never assumed.

approval_decision_id.description: Decision approving an in-cluster GitHub write credential.

https://sortyard.ai/spec/credential-cust.title: CredentialCustody

https://sortyard.ai/spec/decision-log.sc.description: One entry of the DecisionLog, a specialised event stream (§3.8): every conductor decision (claim / skip / hand-back / merge / stall) with the inputs it computed from — policy versions, queue snapshot hash, reason codes — so 'why wasn't X picked up?' is a query.

reason_codes.description: Pickup-preview reason codes, e.g. 'slot held: merging', 'held: parent in backlog', 'throttled: heavy cap full', 'unbound: mirror stale'.

https://sortyard.ai/spec/decision-log.sc.title: DecisionLogEntry

https://sortyard.ai/spec/decision.schema.description: A first-class work type implementing the no-tap doctrine (§3.3): a question for the operator, a recorded default and a decide_by time. Silence past decide_by applies the default and closes the item unattended. Workflows branch on a Decision; they never block on a person.

examples.question: Bundle Plane, fork it, or build the board natively?

default.description: The recorded default, applied when decide_by passes in silence.

task_id.description: Task or chain the decision steers, if any.

https://sortyard.ai/spec/decision.schema.title: Decision

https://sortyard.ai/spec/deployment-conf.description: The Helm values reflected into the UI as the Admin console (§3.9): namespaces, pools, ingress, retention; plus the definitions mode of §5.1 (git mode default for teams, DB-only for small installs) and the secrets backend. Installation-wide, so not workspace-scoped.

control_plane_protection.description: PriorityClass + reserved requests for the control plane and a worker LimitRange (§3.7b honesty correction).

https://sortyard.ai/spec/deployment-conf.title: DeploymentConfig

https://sortyard.ai/spec/escalation.sche.description: An explicit chain stall (§3.3): plain-language reason, stall class, repair attempts. Self-repair gets at most two attempts per distinct defect (class + phase); a repair concluding 'not dispatcher-side' ends after one attempt; redeploy failure and repaired code not running within 15 minutes are terminal.

examples.reason: Build failed the declared whitespace check twice with no change in the record.

phase.description: Stage/phase the defect occurred in; class + phase identifies a distinct defect.

stall_class.description: Names derived from the draft's prose; see NOTES.md (stall classes).

https://sortyard.ai/spec/escalation.sche.title: Escalation

https://sortyard.ai/spec/eval-run.schema.description: One execution of an Eval (§3.8). Records a verdict on observed evidence only; when the eval could not run, the verdict is absent and the eval's absent-state behaviour is recorded.
https://sortyard.ai/spec/eval-run.schema.title: EvalRun

https://sortyard.ai/spec/eval.schema.jso.description: A named, versioned check (§3.8): subject, method, criteria, a mandatory absent-state, a posture (advisory by default; the standing battery never gates) and the resource rule — one heavy eval at a time per host, and eval conditions must not manufacture what they measure.

criteria: current head has a green deploy
examples.name: deployed head is green
examples.subject: product

heavy.description: Heavy evals run one at a time per host.

pack_id.description: Eval pack (Extension) this eval ships in.

https://sortyard.ai/spec/eval.schema.jso.title: Eval

https://sortyard.ai/spec/event.schema.js.description: One entry of the append-only Event Ledger, the system's spine (§3.8): every transition, decision, eval verdict, merge and deploy observation is an Event {ts, actor, object, transition, facts, refs}. OpenTelemetry export is a projection of the ledger.

kind.description: Domain object kind, e.g. task, chain, stage_run, decision.

https://sortyard.ai/spec/event.schema.js.title: Event

https://sortyard.ai/spec/execution-bindi.description: The resolved, verified answer for a (task, stage) pair, produced before the conductor may claim (§3.7b): right workflow, right context, right skills, right place, all dependencies brought to bear, and a bounded blast radius (ResourceEnvelope). An incomplete binding makes the task ineligible with a specific reason code; the task stays visible.

subject.description: Named subject, e.g. skill@version or dependency task id.

https://sortyard.ai/spec/execution-bindi.title: ExecutionBinding

https://sortyard.ai/spec/extension.schem.description: The plugin unit (§3.7a), registered in the Extension Registry, versioned, enable/disable per project. Kinds: Skill (SKILL.md + assets with frontmatter contract), Integration (connector proven locally against doc-derived fixtures — not a live production test), Sensor (scheduled observer that files findings as Tasks, always outside the pipeline, never executes a task), and archetype/workflow/eval packs.

credential_refs.description: User-supplied at runtime via the secrets store.

https://sortyard.ai/spec/extension.schem.title: Extension

https://sortyard.ai/spec/grooming-pass.s.description: A scheduled/agent job (§3.5) that turns findings into tasks, fills depends/priority/placement, orders milestones and verifies pickup-eligibility, and files a defect when a project's eligible queue is empty while known work exists. Judgment work is frontier-model only; a non-frontier run stops and reports the mismatch (recorded as a Policy on the pass).

examples.mismatch_report: Pass dispatched on a non-frontier model; stopped.

https://sortyard.ai/spec/grooming-pass.s.title: GroomingPass

https://sortyard.ai/spec/installation.sc.description: One deployed harness instance (§3.1). Config: cluster, namespaces, storage, ingress, auth provider (OIDC). The root of tenancy, so it carries no workspace_id.
https://sortyard.ai/spec/installation.sc.title: Installation

https://sortyard.ai/spec/integrator.sche.description: The fenced single writer (ship.py successor, §3.7a) that turns a proven delivery into a landed one: it requires a passed proof receipt for the exact (base, candidate) pair, verify approval of the exact head and a tree-identity assertion, then lands via the Git Data API recreating signed commits byte-exact, recording both heads in a register checkpoint. The reboot unifies both of today's integrators on this fenced model. Receives its credential through the installation's configured CredentialCustody.

runs.description: Where the component runs; operator-side by default (no GitHub credential in the cluster).

https://sortyard.ai/spec/integrator.sche.title: Integrator

https://sortyard.ai/spec/lane.schema.jso.description: A concurrency + routing construct (§3.4): max concurrent chains, eligible projects/workflows, host/cluster pool, heavy-job cap. Both of today's cap systems (conductor slots and dispatcher lanes) are Lanes with an explicit scope, because they govern different loops. Tuned live from the Admin console; read at decision time.

scope.description: Which loop the cap governs. See NOTES.md (Lane scope values).

https://sortyard.ai/spec/lane.schema.jso.title: Lane

https://sortyard.ai/spec/milestone.schem.description: Ordered grouping of tasks (§3.3). Milestones run in an explicit per-project order and tasks carry an explicit sequence inside their milestone (§3.3a.1). An unsequenced milestone behind a finished one is shaping debt.

sequenced.description: False marks shaping debt surfaced by grooming.

tasks.description: Task ids in their explicit sequence order.

https://sortyard.ai/spec/milestone.schem.title: Milestone

https://sortyard.ai/spec/mirror.schema.j.description: A read-only repo mirror on a shared volume that workers clone from; jobs never fetch private remotes (§3.7). Source, last refresh and freshness are recorded; a stale mirror is a named failure mode.
https://sortyard.ai/spec/mirror.schema.j.title: Mirror

https://sortyard.ai/spec/operator.schema.description: A human user of the console (§3.9), authenticated through the installation's OIDC provider. Operators are not workflow roles; their permissions come from RoleBindings.
https://sortyard.ai/spec/operator.schema.title: Operator

credential_pool.description: Subscription accounts as pooled resources: selection + failure isolation. Not a lease and not a concurrency limiter.

handback.description: Draft names the kind; the mandatory reason/evidence and 24h re-alert come from §3.3/§3.8. Open otherwise (NOTES.md).

merge_gate.description: Red never merges; absent checks are a coverage gap (record + file ticket + merge on review/local proof); no force-merge ever. Review count is scoped by regime.

fix_rounds.description: Post-#199 fix-round count: UNVERIFIED in the draft (§10). No default is frozen.

model_budget.description: Per-key budgets (budgets live per API key, not in the product) and model/effort selection per stage.

pipeline_purity.description: No delivery-pipeline stage may declare a third-party or deployment-environment dependency; the workflow validator refuses such a workflow.

replica_required.description: Build stages must attach replica adversary-review evidence before push.

retention.description: Draft names the kind only; parameters are open (NOTES.md).

runner.description: No GitHub-hosted runners — estate/self-hosted only; Dependabot is the sole exception.

secrets.description: Secrets only via the secrets store, only into jobs that declare the need, never logged, never in definitions. CredentialCustody records the deliberate exceptions.

stall.description: Stall detection; values from the mh-chain rules in §3.3. Open otherwise (NOTES.md).

https://sortyard.ai/spec/policy.schema.j.description: Every enforceable rule as an object (§3.6): id, scope, kind, parameters, enforcement (refuse | warn | record), absent-state behaviour, version, audit history. Conductor and workers read policy at decision time. Parameters are checked per kind; kinds whose parameters the draft does not specify stay open (see NOTES.md).

audit_history.description: AuditLog entry ids for every change to this policy.

scope_ref.description: Project, workflow or stage the policy applies to when scope is not global.

https://sortyard.ai/spec/policy.schema.j.title: Policy

https://sortyard.ai/spec/prioritization-.description: A strict lexicographic order (§3.5): an ordered list of keys (urgent_flag, milestone_sequence, priority_tier, age), tie-break roles only, per project or global. Weighted scoring / cost_of_delay is a proposed change (§10), not part of this contract. A slot stays occupied by any claimed item that is neither done nor blocked, including merging. Urgent bypasses lane caps and does not count against them.

slot_release_states.description: Claimed items hold their slot until reaching one of these states.

https://sortyard.ai/spec/prioritization-.title: PrioritizationPolicy

https://sortyard.ai/spec/project.schema..description: A product being built (§3.2). Pins an archetype version and inherits archetype updates explicitly (diff + accept).

repos.description: Repo objects belonging to the project; each Repo carries URL, default branch and role.

state.description: Lifecycle discovery → active → maintain → archived, plus the source's project-definition state. See NOTES.md (Project lifecycle).

tracker.description: Tracker pointer: internal by default; an external tracker is optional (§8).

https://sortyard.ai/spec/project.schema..title: Project

https://sortyard.ai/spec/repo.schema.jso.description: A first-class repository (§3.2): connection status, webhook health, runner pool, branch protection posture, last observed HEAD, and explicit role + aliases[] so codename vs product-name drift cannot break automation.
https://sortyard.ai/spec/repo.schema.jso.title: Repo

https://sortyard.ai/spec/resource-envelo.description: The bounded-blast-radius part of every ExecutionBinding (§3.7b): CPU/memory requests and limits on the Job (and its sidecars), a wall-clock deadline whose expiry kills the Job, and a heavy/light classification that admission caps read. An embedded value object of ExecutionBinding; it has no identity of its own.
https://sortyard.ai/spec/resource-envelo.title: ResourceEnvelope

https://sortyard.ai/spec/role-binding.sc.description: Grants a console/API role to an operator or agent service account (§3.9): admin, operator, viewer, agent-service-account. Distinct from workflow Roles (§3.4).
https://sortyard.ai/spec/role-binding.sc.title: RoleBinding

https://sortyard.ai/spec/role.schema.jso.description: Role / Persona: who is asking at a stage (§3.4). Template roles planner, implementer, reviewer, designer (infrastructure omits designer), plus agentic-persona C-suite personas. A role = system-prompt bundle + context allowlist policy + tool permissions + default model policy. 'operator' is not a role.

system_prompt_bundle.description: Path or content ref of the prompt bundle.

https://sortyard.ai/spec/role.schema.jso.title: Role

https://sortyard.ai/spec/scorecard-batte.description: Today's standing eval instrument as a first-class eval pack (§3.8): scored at verify time, advisory and never gating; evidence assembled mechanically from chain facts; taste never machine-graded; supports source-excluded grading; a lone delivery is unscored until a comparable baseline corpus exists.
https://sortyard.ai/spec/scorecard-batte.title: ScorecardBattery

https://sortyard.ai/spec/secret.schema.j.description: A reference, never a value (§3.7a). Points at the secrets store (OpenBao for NonceLogic; external-secrets, sealed-secrets or plain Kubernetes Secrets for OSS installs). The Admin console manages references, scopes and rotation state; values never transit the harness API, so this schema admits no value field.

locator.description: Path/key in the backend, e.g. kv/sortyard/github-app.

https://sortyard.ai/spec/secret.schema.j.title: Secret

https://sortyard.ai/spec/self-heal.schem.description: Hand-back's owning process (§3.8): a handed-back item loses conductor eligibility, gains a self-heal assignment, carries the worker's account of why, and awaits host-access work under the self-heal contract, with re-alerting at 24h dwell.

examples.worker_account: CI log unreadable from the worker pod.

worker_account.description: The worker's account of why it handed back.

https://sortyard.ai/spec/self-heal.schem.title: SelfHeal

https://sortyard.ai/spec/sequence-change.description: Sequence is not a container object; it is a property (`sequence`) of Tasks, Milestones, Workflows and Chains (§3.3, §3.3a). What is recorded as an object is the SequenceChange: an auditable event whenever a human (board drag) or grooming reorders a milestone or a task's sequence — the change, its author and its reason. The Pickup Preview re-derives immediately.

order.description: Which of the five recorded orders changed.

https://sortyard.ai/spec/sequence-change.title: SequenceChange

https://sortyard.ai/spec/sequencing-poli.description: How claim sequences of multiple projects interleave on shared lane capacity (§3.3a.5): strict global order, per-project round-robin, or reserved slots per project. Recorded, applied mechanically, shown in the Pickup Preview.

reserved_slots.description: Project id -> reserved slot count (today's de facto per-project lane caps).

https://sortyard.ai/spec/sequencing-poli.title: SequencingPolicy

https://sortyard.ai/spec/stage-run.schem.description: One stage execution inside a Chain (§3.3): job ref, agent session ref, inputs packet hash, outputs, observed facts, cost, duration. The StageRun must run the exact packet its ExecutionBinding recorded (§3.7b).
https://sortyard.ai/spec/stage-run.schem.title: StageRun

https://sortyard.ai/spec/task.schema.jso.description: The unit of work (§3.3), absorbing today's Plane work item and meta-harness task block into one object. The outcome states what, not how; verification lives in workflows/evals, so there is deliberately no acceptance-test field. Hand-back is a decision with a mandatory reason and evidence, never a label.

examples.outcome: Every §3 object has a JSON Schema in git.
examples.title: Freeze the domain model

examples.handback_reason: CI log unreadable from the worker
examples.outcome: Users land on their dashboard after login.
examples.title: Fix login redirect

board_sequence.description: Board sequence number, the age tie-break key (§3.5).

needs.description: Capabilities/credentials the work requires. A needs-blocked task stays visible; it is simply not eligible (HARNESS-238).

urgent.description: urgent_flag key of the PrioritizationPolicy; urgent bypasses lane caps. See NOTES.md (urgent flag vs urgent tier).

sequence.description: Explicit order inside the milestone (§3.3a.1); pickup reads it.

https://sortyard.ai/spec/task.schema.jso.title: Task

https://sortyard.ai/spec/throughput-wind.description: A retrospective read model over the Event Ledger (§3.8): per hour/day/week and per project/lane/workflow — claims, completions, merges, deploy verdicts, lead and dwell time, lane utilisation, hand-back and stall counts. Recomputable at will; stores nothing authoritative and gates nothing.
https://sortyard.ai/spec/throughput-wind.title: ThroughputWindow

branches_on_decision.description: Branch on a Decision outcome; maps resolution value -> next stage name.

parallel_with.description: Stage names this stage is declared independent of and may run alongside.

https://sortyard.ai/spec/workflow.schema.description: A versioned, declarative stage graph (§3.4). Each stage has a role and an executor type of agent or deterministic; there is deliberately no human-gate executor — humans act through Decision objects. Stage order is the array order; parallelism exists only where a stage declares parallel_with (§3.3a.3). A Chain pins the version it started on.

name.description: Built-ins: feature, incident, release, support (saas-product); change, drift, incident (infrastructure); job; design-first.

https://sortyard.ai/spec/workflow.schema.title: Workflow

https://sortyard.ai/spec/workspace.schem.description: Workspace / Organisation: the tenancy boundary inside an installation (§3.1). v1 runs a single workspace, but every other object carries workspace_id from day one.
https://sortyard.ai/spec/workspace.schem.title: Workspace
